description: Figure 4 is a grouped vertical bar chart illustrating popularity-related quantities across three topical categories (Movies, Songs, Basketball) for multiple language models and three conditions indicated by the legend. The horizontal axis contains the categories Movies, Songs, and Basketball in that left-to-right order, while the vertical axis is labeled “Popularity” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 220 with regularly spaced tick marks at 20-unit intervals. Within each category, bars are grouped by model (Llama3 in blue, Qwen2 in red, ChatGPT in yellow), and for each model there are three adjacent bars corresponding to the legend entries: Pop\_GT (solid color), Pop\_Ge + Q\_GT Ans (lighter tint), and Pop\_Ge + Q\_Ge Ans (lightest tint). In Movies, the bars are relatively short, with approximate values around 30–50 for Llama3 (about 30, 40, 45), around 35–55 for Qwen2 (about 35, 45, 55), and around 20–35 for ChatGPT (about 20, 30, 35). In Songs, the grouped bars are higher, with Llama3 around 50, 70, and 65; Qwen2 around 55, 65, and 85; and ChatGPT around 35, 55, and 70. In Basketball, the bars are tallest overall, with Llama3 around 100, 150, and 165; Qwen2 around 110, 170, and 200; and ChatGPT around 90, 140, and 160. The categories are not shown as explicitly sorted by value, and no individual bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent color/tint encoding and the legend.
